_meta.review_status: DRAFT - general background text written for this project. It must be reviewed and signed off by a qualified clinician before clinical use.
_meta.scope: Background for patients and clinicians reading an AI screening result. Not diagnostic or treatment guidance.

Normal.overview: The classifier did not find patterns it associates with pneumonia or tuberculosis in this chest X-ray.
Normal.typical_xray_findings: Clear lung fields without areas of consolidation, cavities or nodules that the model was trained to recognise.
Normal.what_this_result_means: A 'Normal' result does not rule out disease. Early or subtle disease, and conditions the model was not trained on, can look normal to the classifier.
Normal.typical_next_steps: If symptoms such as persistent cough, fever, weight loss or breathlessness are present, a clinician should assess the patient regardless of this result.

Pneumonia.overview: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs of one or both lungs. It can be caused by bacteria, viruses or fungi.
Pneumonia.typical_xray_findings: Areas of increased opacity (consolidation) in part of a lung, sometimes with air bronchograms or fluid around the lung.
Pneumonia.what_this_result_means: The classifier found patterns similar to the pneumonia images it was trained on. X-ray appearance alone cannot identify the cause, and other conditions can look similar.
Pneumonia.typical_next_steps: A clinician should correlate the image with symptoms, examination and, where appropriate, laboratory tests before deciding on treatment.

Tuberculosis.overview: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection, usually affecting the lungs, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It is curable and preventable.
Tuberculosis.typical_xray_findings: Opacities, nodules or cavities, often in the upper parts of the lungs, sometimes with enlarged lymph nodes or fluid around the lung.
Tuberculosis.what_this_result_means: The classifier found patterns similar to the tuberculosis images it was trained on. A chest X-ray can suggest TB but cannot confirm it.
Tuberculosis.typical_next_steps: TB is confirmed with microbiological tests (for example sputum testing) ordered by a clinician, following local TB guidelines.
